items.proposed: As SERVER without its signed TCP listener; I06 read connection allowed. For I01 only, an AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET listener (HS53): `bind` and `listen`, and `accept4` only with flags 0, SOCK_CLOEXEC, or SOCK_CLOEXEC with SOCK_NONBLOCK, judged on the low 32 bits of the argument because the kernel reads it as an `int` (O-SECCOMP-V5-OBSERVER-LISTENER). Seccomp sees only a descriptor, so it cannot tell the I01 socket from any TCP socket the observer holds or creates (it keeps `socket` for AF_INET and AF_INET6 streams, for the I06 read connection): `bind` and `listen` reach those too, including a `listen` without `bind`, and the TCP-listen boundary is SELinux's (O-W03-OBSERVER-TCP, O-T04-HS53; residual R-OBSERVER-TCP-LISTEN). Among AF_UNIX sockets, too, the filter cannot hold the listener to I01's path; SELinux limits who may connect to the observer's sockets (only the server, `connectto`) and which socket files the observer may create (`planeon_observer_sock_t`). The socket's 0700 directory and its 0600 mode come from the units. The observer binds after its seal and never unlinks: one directory unit keeps /run/planeon/live-proxy for all three listeners, and before the observer starts, systemd removes only its stale I01 path (a pre-start step as init_t, which SELinux matrix v6 permits), so the filter adds no `unlink` (O-W03-OBSERVER-UNIT, O-W03-OBSERVER-PRESTART, O-MATRIX-OBSERVER-SOCK-CLEAR) | `planeon_observer_t`: `name_connect` to `planeon_kubeapi_port_t`; read-only to policy credential; the I01 listener: `create`, `bind`, `listen` and `accept` on its own `unix_stream_socket` (an AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET socket is checked in that class), socket file `planeon_observer_sock_t`, the server its only connector (SELinux matrix v5, `architecture/selinux-matrix-v3/`); no `tcp_socket` `listen` and no `node_bind` (O-W03-OBSERVER-TCP; a later matrix revision closes them in data, O-MATRIX-OBSERVER-TCP) |

Stated residuals:

- R-OBSERVER-TCP-LISTEN: The observer's filter admits bind and listen on every descriptor it holds, including any TCP socket it creates (its filter keeps socket for AF_INET and AF_INET6 streams, for the I06 read connection), because seccomp sees only the descriptor. A listen without bind reaches only SELinux's tcp_socket listen check (v6.12 net/socket.c:1883-1895 calls security_socket_listen, never security_socket_bind), and, by the author's reading of v6.12 SELinux, name_bind is not checked for port 0 or for ports inside ip_local_port_range. So unless the host policy denies planeon_observer_t tcp_socket listen, the observer can open a TCP listener; denying node_bind as well refuses a bind to any TCP port. Follow-up: obligations O-W03-OBSERVER-TCP and O-T04-HS53, then O-MATRIX-OBSERVER-TCP in data (Q-SOL-2).

The data follow in order (Q-SOL-1 (a)): the W02d allowlist successor (`architecture/seccomp-allowlists-v5/`) gains
the OBSERVER I01 listener rule in the same packet as this amendment, then the OBSERVER programs and the edge record
are republished, then R10's HE-004-I01 re-vendors them and serves I01.

dispositions.summary: Two packets: this amendment with seccomp v5, then the OBSERVER programs and the edge record; the stale W02 data pointer names the current successor (H2).
bind and listen unconditional, accept4 with three flag values; the TCP-listen boundary is SELinux's, in W03's policy, T04's check and a later matrix revision; residual R-OBSERVER-TCP-LISTEN.
The socket's directory and mode come from the observer's unit, with no new filter call.
The v1 peer duties stay; HE-004-I01's design decides on HS43's race-free start-time reference.
I01's producer is R10's HE-004-I01; the earlier external-prerequisite statements are superseded for I01.
The shared socket directory (I01, I02, I05): no unit's stop or restart removes another listener's socket, and systemd's handling of it is a T04 question.
The observer binds after its seal and never unlinks; systemd clears a stale I01 path (the directory unit and pre-start step of Q-SOL-7 (a)) under matrix v6's grant to init_t.

One directory unit owns /run/planeon/live-proxy and keeps it; before each listener starts, systemd removes only that listener's own socket path, as init_t; the listener binds after its seal and never unlinks.
W03's file contexts label /run/planeon and its subdirectories planeon_run_t, and T04 checks it.

obligations.label: the allowlist rule
obligations.owner: the W02d allowlist successor v5 (architecture/seccomp-allowlists-v5/), in the same packet as HS53 (Q-SOL-1 (a))
obligations.text: Add to the OBSERVER row of the W02d allowlists, for x86_64 and aarch64, one duty citing HS53's §5.3 OBSERVER row: bind and listen unconditional, and accept4 only when the low 32 bits of argument 3 equal 0, SOCK_CLOEXEC (0x80000) or SOCK_CLOEXEC|SOCK_NONBLOCK (0x80800), so SOCK_NONBLOCK alone and every other bit are killed. Keep the runtime bases and every other role unchanged, and replay the v4 vectors: only OBSERVER's bind, listen and accept4 decisions may change, from KILL_PROCESS to ALLOW.

obligations.label: the socket's directory, mode and freshness
obligations.text: Give I01's socket its required directory, mode and freshness with no new filter call (Q-SOL-3 (a), as refined by Q-SOL-7 (a)). One small directory unit, ordered before the three listeners (observer, broker, gate) and pulled in by each (After= and Requires= on it), owns /run/planeon/live-proxy: RuntimeDirectory= with RuntimeDirectoryPreserve=yes and mode 0700, root:root. The listener units do not list that directory, so no listener's stop or restart removes it or another listener's live socket (Q-SOL-5 (a)); the directory holds I01's policy-observer.sock, I02's capacity-broker.sock and I05's effect-admission.sock. The observer's unit has UMask=0177, so the socket that bind creates is root:root 0600, and no socket activation (native profile v3 forbids sockets created elsewhere). The observer binds after its seal and never unlinks (owner decision SOL-SYSTEMD-CLEANS, for the gate, the broker and the observer alike); for a fresh bind at each start, systemd removes only the observer's own fixed socket path before it starts (ExecStartPre= `rm -f /run/planeon/live-proxy/policy-observer.sock`, running as init_t under matrix v6's grant, O-MATRIX-OBSERVER-SOCK-CLEAR; that it runs as init_t is O-W03-OBSERVER-PRESTART). W03's file contexts label /run/planeon and its subdirectories planeon_run_t; T04 checks it (Q-MX6-R6: systemd creates RuntimeDirectory= paths with the labels its file contexts give, which take precedence over the matrix's named type transition). The I01 socket file is labelled planeon_observer_sock_t by W03's rule for it (matrix v5 leaves that rule to W03; without it the observer's bind is refused, which fails safe). The observer's filter adds no unlink, umask, fchmod or fchmodat call.

obligations.label: the pre-start removal runs as init_t
obligations.owner: W03 (the observer's unit and the host policy), checked by T04
obligations.text: The observer unit's ExecStartPre= step that removes the stale I01 socket path runs as init_t: the host policy gives no domain transition on that exec, so the removal uses matrix v6's init_t grant on planeon_observer_sock_t and nothing else. The step runs in the observer's unit, so that unit's cgroup and limits apply to it; it ends before the observer starts, and the native profile's per-cgroup captures are taken from the running observer, not during the step. If T04 finds that the step runs in another domain, the question goes back to the lane monitor and then the owner (Q-SOL-7 (a)).

obligations.label: no TCP listener for the observer
obligations.text: Give planeon_observer_t no tcp_socket listen and no node_bind (name_bind is already closed by matrix v5), so a bind or listen that the observer's filter admits on a TCP socket is refused by SELinux, including on port 0 and on ports inside ip_local_port_range, where name_bind is not checked (Q-SOL-2 (a)).

obligations.label: native confirmation
obligations.text: On the enrolled kernel and policy, confirm: the observer's installed filter is the v5 OBSERVER program; accept4 on the I01 socket with flags 0, SOCK_CLOEXEC and SOCK_CLOEXEC|SOCK_NONBLOCK succeeds, and with SOCK_NONBLOCK alone kills the observer; an AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET socket is checked in the unix_stream_socket class (the author's reading of v6.12 socket_type_to_security_class); the installed policy gives planeon_observer_t no tcp_socket listen and no node_bind, and a TCP listen by the observer is refused, in each of these cases on AF_INET and AF_INET6: listen without bind, bind to port 0 then listen, and bind to a port inside ip_local_port_range then listen; the socket's directory is root:root 0700 and the socket root:root 0600, and no socket activation is used; no unit's stop or restart removes another listener's live socket (observer, broker or gate): the directory unit keeps /run/planeon/live-proxy (RuntimeDirectoryPreserve=yes) and the listener units do not list it; before the observer's next bind its pre-start step removes only its own stale I01 path and runs as init_t, with no domain transition on that exec, and the installed policy gives init_t on planeon_observer_sock_t only matrix v6's getattr and unlink; /run/planeon and its subdirectories are labelled planeon_run_t by W03's file contexts, and the I01 socket file planeon_observer_sock_t; and the installed filter still kills unlinkat (and unlink on x86_64; aarch64 has no unlink syscall) (Q-SOL-5 (a), SOL-SYSTEMD-CLEANS, Q-SOL-7 (a)).

obligations.label: the observer's TCP listen closed in data
obligations.owner: the next SELinux matrix revision after matrix v6 (matrix v6 does not take it up, Q-SOL-2 (a); its one reopening added only systemd's socket-file grant, SOL-SYSTEMD-CLEANS)
obligations.text: Add tcp_socket listen and node_bind to the matrix's closed permissions for planeon_observer_t, with an assertion that the observer holds neither, so the boundary O-W03-OBSERVER-TCP sets in host policy is also checked in data.

obligations.label: systemd's grant to clear a stale I01 path (met once matrix v6 is adopted)
obligations.owner: SELinux matrix v6 (architecture/selinux-matrix-v4/, SELINUX-MATRIX-V6 candidate 7, which passed its review round 7, recorded in its status at adoption; owner decision SOL-SYSTEMD-CLEANS), whose packet precedes this one
obligations.text: Under matrix v5 only planeon_observer_t and planeon_server_t may unlink planeon_observer_sock_t, and init_t may not even stat it, so systemd could not clear a stale I01 path. Matrix v6 grants init_t sock_file getattr and unlink on the four planeon listener socket files, planeon_observer_sock_t among them, and nothing else on them (its assertions A78 and A79); the directory permissions the removal needs are v5's grants on planeon_run_t. Met once matrix v6 is adopted; this amendment's packet re-checks that the grant is on its base.

obligations.label: the OBSERVER programs and the edge record
obligations.owner: the parallel lane's next harness-onion packet (packet 2 of SECCOMP-OBSERVER-LISTENER, Q-SOL-1 (a))
obligations.text: Republish the OBSERVER's two compiled programs (x86_64 and aarch64) from seccomp v5 and the edge record that binds them for HE-004, as PROGRAMS-REPUBLISH did for EFFECT_GATE; no other role's program changes. The edge record takes the next free version: Q-SOL-1 (a) named edge v5, and the monitor's note with F-SOL-1 says v5 belongs to native-profile v4's edge record (slot 246), so it is probably v6.

obligations.label: the observer serves I01
obligations.owner: R10's HE-004-I01 (primary lane; obligation I01-1 of W03-PLAN-AMEND-2)

supersedes.replacement: as SERVER without its signed TCP listener; the I06 read connection (connect); and, in seccomp v5, the I01 listener of W01 §5.3 as amended by HS53 (bind, listen, and accept4 with flags 0, SOCK_CLOEXEC or SOCK_CLOEXEC|SOCK_NONBLOCK)

residuals.text: The observer's filter admits bind and listen on every descriptor it holds, including any TCP socket it creates (its filter keeps socket for AF_INET and AF_INET6 streams, for the I06 read connection), because seccomp sees only the descriptor. A listen without bind reaches only SELinux's tcp_socket listen check (v6.12 net/socket.c:1883-1895 calls security_socket_listen, never security_socket_bind), and, by the author's reading of v6.12 SELinux, name_bind is not checked for port 0 or for ports inside ip_local_port_range. So unless the host policy denies planeon_observer_t tcp_socket listen, the observer can open a TCP listener; denying node_bind as well refuses a bind to any TCP port.
residuals.followUp: obligations O-W03-OBSERVER-TCP and O-T04-HS53, then O-MATRIX-OBSERVER-TCP in data
